subject: Dedicated capacity sizing follow-up / FinSight
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.inference>
To: Samir Patel <samir.patel@finsight.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.inference>
Date: Tue, 10 Mar 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Recap + sizing questions  Dedicated capacity (FinSight)

Hi Samir 

Thanks again for taking the call earlier. Quick recap and a few follow-up questions so we can size Dedicated capacity accurately:

Recap from today's call:
- Use case: realtime customer-facing analytics (query -> multi-turn LLM responses + light post-processing).
- Preferred deployment: Dedicated capacity (isolation + predictable throughput). Possible Private/VPC later for PHI.
- Initial model family: planning to evaluate Llama-3 70B-style variants (quantized) and a smaller candidate for lower-latency fallbacks.

Sizing / qualification items we need from your end: please reply with approximate values for each so we can propose a config. If you don't have exact numbers, ballpark ranges are fine.

1) Traffic profile
   - Peak requests per second (RPS) / TPS during peak minute: 
   - Sustained RPS (average):
   - Expected daily/weekly seasonality (any spikes):

2) Concurrency and latency expectations
   - Expected concurrent active requests at peak:
   - SLO: p95 latency target for full response (e.g., <500ms, <1s)

3) Token mix (avg per request)
   - Avg prompt tokens in (including system + history):
   - Avg generation tokens out:
   - Percent of requests that are short (<200 tokens) vs long (>1k tokens):

4) Model and accuracy needs
   - Primary model (or family) to serve on Dedicated
   - Need for fallback smaller model for low-cost, low-latency paths?

5) Hardware preference / constraints
   - Any strong preference: H100, A100-80GB, or cost-driven to A10/A30?
   - Important budget constraints to flag to infra/ops team

6) Operational requirements
   - Data residency / VPC / on-prem requirement now vs later
   - Need for guaranteed burst capacity above reserved baseline

Attachments: I attached a short draft Mutual Action Plan (FinSight_MAP_draft.pdf) with milestones and an initial list of deliverables.

Next steps:
- If you can reply with the above by EOD Wednesday, well run a preliminary sizing and propose 2 configs (cost-optimized and performance-optimized).
- We'll also propose a short perf test you can run (we'll provide test harness) to validate throughput on your side.

Thanks  talk soon.
—
Aditya Rao
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
aditya@redwood.inference

From: Samir Patel <samir.patel@finsight.ai>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.inference>
Cc: Emily Chen <emily.chen@finsight.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.inference>
Date: Wed, 11 Mar 2026 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Recap + sizing questions  Dedicated capacity (FinSight)

Hi Aditya / Marissa 

Thanks for the follow-up. Below are the best estimates we have right now after syncing with infra and product:

1) Traffic profile
   - Peak RPS: ~12 requests/sec (short spikes up to ~18 for <5 minutes during ET morning batch)
   - Sustained RPS: ~46 requests/sec (daily average)
   - Seasonality: Friday mornings and promotional days cause ~1.5x traffic for 23 hours

2) Concurrency and latency expectations
   - Concurrent active requests at peak: ~4060 (we estimate 50 concurrent active sessions)
   - SLO: p95 end-to-end response <= 800ms (hard requirement), p99 <= 1.5s desirable

3) Token mix (avg per request)
   - Avg prompt tokens (including history): ~250 tokens
   - Avg generation tokens: ~600 tokens
   - Distribution: ~65% medium (200800 tokens), ~25% short (<200), ~10% long (>1k)

4) Model and accuracy needs
   - Primary: Llama-3-class 70B quantized (best quality) for priority routes
   - Fallback: 13B quantized model for lower-cost routes and non-critical traffic

5) Hardware preference / constraints
   - Prefer H100 if the delta vs A100 isn't >25% cost increase  we value lower latency during peak. If H100 cost is materially higher, A100-80GB is acceptable.

6) Operational requirements
   - Initially Dedicated in our AWS account (we want dedicated tenancy + network isolation). VPC option for later phase; not immediate need.
   - Burst support: yes  want ability to burst up to +50% above baseline for short windows (210 minutes)

We can run any perf harness you provide. We have a staging environment that can run the load tests (non-prod keys available).

Let us know if you need sample payloads or a more detailed token histogram  we can export logs.

Cheers,
Samir
VP Product
FinSight Analytics
samir.patel@finsight.ai
\

From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.inference>
To: Samir Patel <samir.patel@finsight.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.inference>
Date: Thu, 12 Mar 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Recap + sizing questions  Dedicated capacity (FinSight)

Samir 

This is great  thanks for the detailed numbers. Based on your inputs, here are two starter configs we typically propose for FinSight-style workloads. These are preliminary and we'll refine after perf tests.

Option A  Performance-optimized (target p95 < 800ms)
- Base nodes: 4 x H100 (80GB) or A100-80GB equivalent
- Expected steady RPS handling: ~68 RPS for Llama-3-70B quantized (with autoscaling headroom to 1216 RPS for short bursts)
- Concurrency: supports ~50 concurrent active requests with request queueing/priority policies
- Token throughput: ~2M tokens/minute aggregate on base cluster (approx)
- Cost: higher Opex but meets latency SLOs

Option B  Cost-optimized (with fallback routing)
- Base nodes: 6 x A100-80GB (or mix: 4 A100 + 2 A10 for cheaper fallbacks)
- Primary routes serve 70B quantized at reduced concurrency; non-critical routes routed to 13B fallbacks to reduce tokens on big models
- Sustained RPS handling: ~810 RPS across mix with scaled concurrency
- Burst policy: allow +50% burst using reserved burst pool
- Cost: materially lower monthly cost, slightly higher average latency on heavy peak

Notes / questions:
- We should validate exact tokens/sec for your quantized artifacts. If you can provide a representative trace (anonymized) or sample payloads, well run our perf harness and return numbers for each GPU type.
- For H100 vs A100: H100 will give better p95 and improved batch consolidation; we can quantify after perf test.
- For concurrency: we can tune per-route concurrency limits to keep small requests fast while batching long requests efficiently.

Next steps I propose:
1) You drop a small anonymized sample of 200 requests (prompt+expected generation) or a token histogram  well run the perf harness against both model candidates and return measured RPS, p95, and token/sec for A100/H100.
2) Schedule a short 45-minute sizing call with our infra lead (Marissa) and your infra/product team  propose Tue 17 Mar 10:0010:45 PT?
3) We'll produce a final sizing recommendation + cost estimate and a 2-week validation plan.

I attached a short perf test README (perf_test_instructions.md) with how to run in your staging env.

If Tue the 17th doesn't work, propose alternatives and Ill loop in Marissa to lock a time.


Aditya Rao
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
aditya@redwood.inference
